tags.name: Yatouche
tags.qa_notes: RE-AUDIT 2026-08-09: UNRESOLVED jurisdiction stands — no Jordanian dive operator lists this site; all sources continue to place it at Eilat, Israel, north of Coral Beach. Vessel history CORRECTED: prior note called it an 'Israeli military gunboat' — two independent sources (ahla-dive.com, and corroborating aggregation) instead describe the Yatush as a former U.S. Navy patrol vessel that served off Vietnam and was transferred to Israel after the American withdrawal, then used by the Israeli Navy until it was sunk as an artificial reef (sources disagree whether this was the mid-1980s or 1994 — not resolved, stated as a range). Depth confirmed 27-33m (stern ~24-26m, bow ~30-33m) — deeper than our 20-25m depth fields; flagging as a further data-quality concern on top of the jurisdiction issue. Length reported as 58m in one source — not independently cross-checked. Coordinates and depth field NOT updated in this pass because the site's Jordanian status itself remains unconfirmed; do not present as a confirmed Jordanian dive site.

tags.name: Cedar Pride
tags.qa_notes: RE-AUDIT 2026-08-09: All core facts re-confirmed across 5 independent domains. Built 1964, S.A. Juliana Constructora shipyard, Gijon, Spain. Names: Mone Dos -> Puerto De Pasajes -> San Bruno -> Cedar Pride. Length 74m consistently reported (one source loosely describes 'around 80m' for overall wreck extent, not hull length). Tonnage: every source found in this pass reports 1,161 GRT/tons; the ~2,500t alternate figure flagged in the prior QA pass (2026-06-10) could NOT be reproduced from any source in this re-audit — treating 1,161 GRT as the sourced figure and removing the unresolved-conflict framing from the markdown (CORRECTION). Fire 2 Aug 1982 (2 crew fatalities), scuttled 16 Nov 1985 by Crown Prince Abdullah (later King Abdullah II), confirmed. Lies on port side, ~10m-27m. Marine life (site-specific, re-confirmed): lionfish, giant frogfish, clownfish, snapper, fusiliers, angelfish, moray eels, hawksbill turtles.

tags.name: סופה
tags.qa_notes: RE-AUDIT 2026-08-09: UNRESOLVED jurisdiction stands. Sufa/Satil (INS Sufa, Sa'ar 3-class missile boat, 46m) re-confirmed by all sources as located at Village Beach/Coral Beach, Eilat, Israel, not Jordan. Sinking-year conflict persists: adrex.com states 1994; a second source (Mares dive blog) states 1993. Both are credible dive-industry sources — conflict is stated, not resolved. Depth ~20-25m re-confirmed. No Jordanian dive operator lists this wreck.

tags.name: Japanese Gardens Coral Reefs
tags.qa_notes: RE-AUDIT 2026-08-09: Reef profile re-confirmed (shallow 1-2m start, Black Coral Valley 26-30m, gorgonian fan ~23m). Coral relocation history STRENGTHENED with a National Geographic feature and peer-reviewed source (Al-Dirreh/Saudi-border corals moved ~2012-2013 ahead of port construction; ~7,000 colonies transplanted; >87% survival rate) - upgrades this from a single-source claim to multi-source (incl. academic literature). Marine life (site-specific): hawksbill turtles, eagle rays (newly corroborated by arabdivers.jo), sergeant majors, fusiliers, moray eels, lionfish, anthias. The 'occasional white-tip reef sharks' claim from the prior pass was NOT re-confirmed in this pass's sources (not contradicted either) - retained but flagged as single-source.

tags.name: Gorgon 1
tags.qa_notes: RE-AUDIT 2026-08-09: CONFLICT FOUND - the prior QA pass (2026-06-10) asserted 'two large gorgonian fan corals' as corrected fact. Re-pulling sources in this pass, arabdivers.jo (site's own operator page) now describes 'a single, massive gorgonian fan coral' while jordan-travel.com independently states 'two large Gorgonia corals.' This is a genuine source conflict, not resolved either way - CORRECTING the markdown from an assertive 'two fans' claim to explicitly note the discrepancy. Three pinnacles rising to surface and house-sized cabbage coral at base of third pinnacle re-confirmed. Marine life (site-specific, expanded): hawksbill turtles, big-eye emperors, sergeant majors, fusiliers, glassfish, lionfish, stonefish, yellowmouth moray, plus cleaner shrimp and grouper newly confirmed via arabdivers.jo. Boat access primary, re-confirmed.

tags.name: Tank
tags.qa_notes: RE-AUDIT 2026-08-09: All facts re-confirmed, no changes. M42 Duster anti-aircraft vehicle, sunk 1 Sep 1999 by the Jordanian Royal Ecological Diving Society, cleaned of hazardous materials before sinking. 6m depth, ~20m from shore. Specific years of prior Jordanian Army service still NOT independently confirmed by any source in this pass either - the earlier decision to remove the '1965 to 1998' service-date claim stands. Marine life (site-specific): lionfish, angelfish, groupers, moray eels.

tags.name: Plane wreck
tags.qa_notes: RE-AUDIT 2026-08-09: All facts re-confirmed across 5 domains including a new maritime/diving trade source (divernet.com). Lockheed C-130 Hercules, donated by Royal Jordanian Air Force, scuttled 16 Nov 2017 (300m from shoreline per divernet.com - new detail added). Length 30m, wingspan ~40m, max depth 17m, tail rises to ~5m. Plastic skeleton in pilot seat re-confirmed. March 2020 storm damage re-confirmed: fuselage torn apart, wings separated, tail section broadly intact. 2017 sinking date re-confirmed against the earlier flagged 2021 discrepancy.

tags.name: Rainbow reef
tags.qa_notes: RE-AUDIT 2026-08-09: All facts re-confirmed, no changes. Arc-shaped reef, 6-25m+ (arabdivers.jo gives a slightly wider range than the previously recorded 6-18m). Four telecommunications cables laid 1996 (Jordan-Egypt) re-confirmed; northern wall is an artificial reef structure protecting the cables. Aqaba's top night dive site re-confirmed by multiple sources. Marine life (site-specific): Spanish dancers, lobsters, feather stars, moray eels, lionfish, parrotfish, butterflyfish, wrasse, scorpionfish, eagle rays.

tags.name: אתר צלילה -סטי"ל (24 מטר)
tags.qa_notes: RE-AUDIT 2026-08-09: Coordinate/jurisdiction CRITICAL flag unchanged and unresolved - OSM coordinates and Hebrew name tag ('Diving site - Satil (24m)') still strongly indicate this entry is the Israeli Satil/Sufa wreck at Eilat, not Jordan's actual Underwater Military Museum off South Beach, Aqaba. The museum content itself re-confirmed and refined: 21 decommissioned Royal Jordanian Army vehicles (both blooloop.com and CNN independently give 21, tightening the prior '19-21' hedge), arranged across a ~140m span on the seabed (new detail). Depth breakdown refined: ~2 pieces at ~5m, ~8 pieces at 15-20m, ~11 pieces at 20-28m (broadly consistent with, and more granular than, the prior 5-28m range). Two Bell AH-1F Cobra helicopters at 25-28m re-confirmed as the deepest/centerpiece items. Inaugurated 25 Jul 2019 by ASEZA, re-confirmed. Marine life (site-specific): garden eels, moray eels, scorpionfish, bannerfish, reef fish, nudibranchs.

Depth 18m and medium-strong currents re-confirmed. Site identification remains moderate confidence (coordinate-based match, not a named/mapped confirmation from the source).
